pull.title: KAFKA-21389: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED
pull.body:
The group coordinator returns `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED` in two situations:
during the initial rebalance delay of a new streams group, and when it
defers computing a new target assignment because the configured
assignment interval has not elapsed yet. In the second case the member
keeps its current assignment, but `StreamsMembershipManager` mapped the
status to `isGroupReady=false`. The membership manager then
re-reconciled the unchanged tasks as not ready, and `StreamThread`
skipped processing, committing and punctuating for all owned tasks until
a later heartbeat (up to one heartbeat interval) no longer carried the
status.

With this change, `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED` on its own keeps the readiness of
the previous target assignment. Since the target assignment starts out
not ready and is reset when the member leaves or is fenced, a member
that has not been ready yet, including one waiting out the initial
rebalance delay, still does not enter `RUNNING` with an empty
assignment. A ready member keeps processing the tasks it owns. Missing
or incorrectly partitioned topics still mark the group as not ready,
also when reported together with `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED`.

The new unit tests in `StreamsMembershipManagerTest` reproduce the issue
(a ready member owning a task receiving a second tasks-assigned event
with `isGroupReady=false`) and cover the combination with a
missing-topics status. The existing test for a ready/not-ready
transition without task changes now uses `MISSING_SOURCE_TOPICS`, since
it previously asserted the behaviour being fixed.

Reviewers: ChickenchickenLove <ojt90902@naver.com>

review_comments.body:
Could we add two more test cases to cover the readiness preservation here?
- `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED` while an assignment callback is pending. Start with `currentAssignment.isGroupReady != targetAssignment.isGroupReady`, receive a delayed response, then complete the pending callback and generate the ACK. Verify that the latest target readiness is preserved, with no additional assignment callback. Covering both directions would distinguish the intended behavior from accidentally using `currentAssignment.isGroupReady`; the current tests have already completed reconciliation when the delayed response arrives.
- `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED` with a non-null, unchanged assignment while `STABLE`. Complete reconciliation, generate the `ACK` to transition to `STABLE`, then receive the delayed response with the same task sets. Verify that the member stays ready and `STABLE` without another assignment callback. This matches a possible broker response: it echoes the assignment when owned tasks are reported, even while computing the next target assignment is delayed.

What do you think?

Agreed, both are worth pinning down. Added `testAssignmentDelayedWhileReconcilingKeepsTargetReady` / `...KeepsTargetNotReady` for the pending-callback case in both directions (both fail if the readiness is taken from `currentAssignment`), and `testAssignmentDelayedWithUnchangedAssignmentKeepsStableMemberReady` for the echoed assignment while `STABLE`, which also fails without the fix.

commit.message:
MINOR: Keep a ready streams member ready on ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED

The group coordinator returns ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED both during the initial
rebalance delay of a new group and when it defers computing a new target
assignment because of the configured assignment interval. In the second
case the member keeps its current assignment, but the client mapped the
status to isGroupReady=false, which made the StreamThread stop processing
all owned tasks until a later heartbeat no longer carried the status.

ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED now keeps the readiness of the previous target
assignment. A member that has not been ready yet, including one waiting
out the initial rebalance delay, stays not ready, while a ready member
keeps processing. Missing or incorrectly partitioned topics still mark
the group as not ready, also when reported together with
ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED.
